Job Posting: Environmental Scientist (Compliance)

Military Department

JC-538302



Environmental Scientist (Compliance)
  
ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,551.00 - $9,787.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **11/20/2026**

**Application Methods:**

Electronic (Using your CalCareer Account)

By Mail

Drop-off

Print Job

Save Job

### **Job Description and Duties**

The Environmental Programs Directorate supports current and future mission requirements of the CMD by assisting units, programs, and leaders to comply with environmental laws, regulations, and policy while promoting environmental stewardship at military training sites and facilities.

  

Under the general direction of the Training Site Branch Chief and Compliance Program Manager, this position supports the CMD’s Compliance Program at Camp Roberts (CR) with regular assignments to Camp San Luis Obispo (CSLO) and quarterly visits to Joint Forces Training Base (JFTB). Duties are broad-based and include, but are not limited to, management of the following media areas: hazardous materials and hazardous waste, stormwater, drinking water, wastewater, underground and above-ground storage tanks, landfills, solid waste/recycling, air quality, and other related programs. The position requires occasional travel in-state and out of-state.

  

Effective July 1, 2025, specific Bargaining Units and associated Excluded State employees are subject to a salary reduction between 2% - 4.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025) hours each month. For more details about PLP 2025, visit the California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) website.

  

This posting may be used to fill future vacancies in accordance with 2 CCR §249.3

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

Working location: Camp Roberts (Hwy 101, Bldg 910, Camp Roberts, CA 93451) and San Luis Obispo (10 Sonoma Ave, San Luis Obispo CA 93405)
  
  
Visa Sponsorship: CMD is not an E-Verify employer and does not offer visa sponsorship. All applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of appointment.

**CMD supports a hybrid telework schedule for many positions, consistent with operational requirements.**

The telework policy is subject to change, and additional in-office days may be required and/or minimal notification may be given to report to the worksite if an urgent need arises.

### **Department Information**

The California Military Department is a diverse, community-based organization comprised of four pillars: the California Army National Guard, the California Air National Guard, the California State Military Reserve and the California Youth and Community Programs. Across our organization, we are committed to improving, preparing and protecting our communities, state and nation.
  
  
The California Military Department (CMD) is committed to fostering a professional, inclusive, and mission-driven work environment where all employees are valued, respected, and empowered to succeed. We are dedicated to providing positive opportunities for growth, development, and advancement.
  
  
Employees working for the California Military Department (CMD) are subject to the provisions of California Military and Veterans Code § 398.

Department Website: http://www.calguard.ca.gov/

### **Special Requirements**

* The position(s) require(s) a valid California Drivers License (CDL). You must answer the questions addressing your CDL on your application. Ensure you provide your CDL number, class, expiration date, and any endorsements and/or restrictions.
* The position(s) require(s) a Background Investigation be cleared prior to being hired.

Employment History on the STD 678 must be complete and include dates, accurate hours per week, total time worked, duties and responsibilities, and contact names and phone numbers of supervisors.
  
  
Real ID Act: Effective May 31, 2025, and in accordance with the Real ID Act of 2005, access to all military installations will require a REAL ID compliant driver’s license or identification card issued by the DMV. Individuals who do not have a REAL ID must present one of the following acceptable alternative documents: a valid U.S. passport, a certified birth certificate, or an active or retired military ID.
  
  
For more information about the Real ID Act of 2005, visit Congress.gov For details on how to apply for a REAL ID, visit DMV.ca.gov.
  
  
This position requires background investigation and the issuance and continued possession of a Department of Defense (DoD) Common Access Card (CAC), as a condition of employment. The CAC is required to access certain facilities, systems, or information necessary to perform the duties of the position.

jobs.title: Director, Head of Investigative Toxicology
jobs.description:
**Director, Head of Investigative Toxicology**

*Build Nurix's in-house in vitro toxicology capability from the ground up. As Director, Head of Investigative Toxicology, you'll establish the assays, infrastructure and mechanistic understanding to identify target- and modality-related safety liabilities earlier in discovery, shaping lead selection for our growing pipeline of targeted protein degrader programs. This is a hands-on, lab-based leadership role.*

  

**Position Description**

**The Opportunity**

Nurix Therapeutics is seeking a Head of Investigative Toxicology to establish and lead our in-house in vitro toxicology testing capability. Reporting into the Preclinical Toxicology leadership team, this individual will build the assays, infrastructure, and mechanistic understanding needed to characterize target- and modality-related safety liabilities earlier in discovery, reducing reliance on external CROs for early screening and de-risking. This is a hands-on, lab-based leadership role for a scientist who wants to build a function from the ground up, working in close partnership with Discovery Biology, Chemistry, DMPK, and Pharmacology to inform lead selection and optimization for our growing pipeline of targeted protein degrader programs. The position reports to the Senior Vice President, Nonclinical Toxicology.

***In Vitro Toxicology Capability Build***

* Design, establish, and validate an in-house in vitro toxicology testing platform, including assay selection, equipment procurement, protocol development, and standard operating procedures
* Develop and implement in vitro toxicology (primary and immortalized cell culture, hepatocyte and iPSC cardiomyocyte models) assays to screen for cytotoxicity and off-target liabilities
* Define the technical roadmap and prioritize which in vitro assays to bring in-house versus continue to source through CRO partners, balancing scientific value, cost, and speed
* Own day-to-day lab operations for the function, including equipment maintenance, vendor and reagent management, and data management systems

***Investigative & Mechanistic Toxicology***

* Serve as the in vitro/investigative toxicology representative on discovery project teams, providing mechanistic insight into target and modality-related safety findings
* Design and interpret investigative studies to elucidate mechanisms of toxicity, including neosubstrate and off-target degradation risk relevant to targeted protein degrader molecules
* Partner with DMPK, Pharmacology, and Discovery Biology to integrate in vitro toxicology data into candidate selection, structure-activity relationship (SAR), and lead optimization decisions
* Translate in vitro findings into risk assessments and clear recommendations for project teams and research leadership

***Team & Culture***

* Hire, mentor, and develop scientific staff as the in vitro toxicology function grows
* Represent in vitro/investigative toxicology in Research Leadership meetings and contribute to the broader nonclinical safety strategy
* Foster a collaborative, science-driven culture consistent with Nurix's values of rigor, creativity, and patient focus

  

**What You'll Bring**

***Required Qualifications***

* PhD in Toxicology, Pharmacology, Molecular Biology, or a closely related life sciences discipline; postdoctoral training preferred
* 10+ years of relevant nonclinical safety, investigative toxicology, or molecular/cellular toxicology experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, including direct, hands-on laboratory experience with in vitro and/or complex in vitro (MPS) model systems
* Demonstrated experience building, validating, and implementing new in vitro assay platforms or laboratory capabilities in an industry setting
* Strong working knowledge of mechanisms of drug-induced toxicity and the in vitro tools used to investigate them (e.g., high content imaging, primary and immortalized cell culture, hepatocyte/cardiomyocyte models, genotoxicity assays)
* Proven ability to translate in vitro data into actionable risk assessments and communicate findings clearly to cross-functional project teams and senior leadership
* Experience managing CRO relationships and evaluating build-versus-buy decisions for laboratory capabilities

***Preferred Qualifications***

* Experience with targeted protein degradation (TPD) or other novel small molecule modalities, including neosubstrate/off-target degradation risk assessment
* Experience establishing or scaling a laboratory function within a growing, clinical-stage biotech
* Familiarity with New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) and organ-on-chip/microphysiological systems
* People management or mentoring experience
* Strong publication record in investigative or molecular toxicology

  

**Salary Range:** $240,100 - $281,700

*The posted range applies to roles based in the San Francisco Bay Area and reflects local market conditions. Where an offer lands within that range depends on the candidate's relevant experience, technical expertise, and how their background aligns with the role's requirements.*

**Location:** Onsite – Brisbane, CA

  

**Fit with Nurix Culture and Values**

* Strong team orientation; highly collaborative
* Solutions and results-oriented focus
* Hands-on approach; resourceful and open to diverse points of view

  

**About Nurix Therapeutics**

*Nurix Therapeutics is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of targeted protein degradation medicines, the next frontier in innovative drug design aimed at improving treatment options for patients with cancer and inflammatory diseases. Powered by a fully AI-integrated discovery engine capable of tackling any protein class, and coupled with unparalleled ligase expertise, Nurix's dedicated team has built a formidable advantage in translating the science of targeted protein degradation into clinical advancements.
